dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (日医標準レセプトソフト); GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL-based system used in Japanese medical clinics. Program ORCGW11 handles system management information settings, specifically printer assignment configuration.
evidence: EXEC CICS/SQL absent; MCP-STATUS/MCP-EVENT pattern typical of ORCA MCP framework
58 COPY statements referencing ORCA-specific copybooks (CPSK1030.INC, CPSK1031.INC, etc.)
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING MCPAREA SPAAREA LINKAREA SCRAREA

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA standard medical receipt (レセプト) software — system management information settings subsystem, specifically printer name assignment and window/screen management for clinic administrative use
purpose.summary: ORCGW11 is a screen-handling subprogram within the JMA ORCA medical receipt system that manages system configuration settings, particularly printer assignment and related output destination configuration. It processes screen transitions, initializes SPA (scratchpad area) data, performs entry validation, and drives a window-based UI via the MCP framework. It is called as a linked subprogram and returns control via EXIT PROGRAM.

notable_features: Heavy use of COPY statements (58) for ORCA framework copybooks
MCP (Message Control Program) event-driven screen framework (MCP-STATUS, MCP-EVENT, MCP-WINDOW)
SPA (Scratchpad Area) pattern for inter-program state passing
LINKAGE SECTION with MCPAREA, SPAAREA, LINKAREA, SCRAREA
EVALUATE MCP-STATUS ALSO MCP-EVENT dispatch pattern
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — uses proprietary ORCA DB access layer (MCPDATA.INC, CPORCMCP.INC)
Revision history spanning 2000–2006 with multiple contributors
verdict.notes: File decoded as latin-1 but comments are Japanese EUC-JP encoded, causing mojibake in the displayed text. The program is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA system. Truncated at 16000 chars out of ~149741 bytes (3645 lines); full procedure division not visible but structure is clear from what is shown.
